profiles.title: CFP Standard
profiles.variant: Eight-zone CFP Standard front fascia and Main Control PCB — DFU7001020 Rev 2 / DFU7004010 Rev 1
profiles.scope: Source-backed operator and access-level-3 practice: remove the simulated cover, use SW8, program documented zone/output functions, and read the engineering diagnostic indications.
limitations: A fictional eight-zone CFP Standard training configuration, not an electrical panel model or a live system connection.
The removable-cover view represents the Main Control PCB documented in Figure 12; it does not invent a full power-supply or mains interior.
The manual marks coincidence and non-latching operation as non-compliant with EN54-2. Their presence in the trainer is not approval for an installation.
Only the documented configuration relationships are represented. Coupled edge cases, electrical thresholds, detector protocols and analogue circuit behaviour are outside the simulation.

Test timing is an approximate training-clock demonstration. Page 15 describes pulsing Test/zone indicators while page 17 describes them as steady after leaving programming; that source difference is retained rather than treated as a universal firmware timing specification.
Closing the training cover does not press Escape Access or change stored engineering settings. Any simulator draft handling is distinct from a verified lid sensor or firmware behaviour.
This is the Standard fascia/edition. Similar Economy or AlarmSense cabinets do not establish compatibility.

features.title: Access level 1 / 2
features.description: Use the real numbered keys for the documented 2 1 4 3 code, or the simulated keyswitch. The separate sounder/reset keys are not the numbered access keys.

features.title: Indicator test

features.title: Alarm and reset
features.description: An unsilenced fire flashes the general/zone indicators. Silence leaves a steady indication; reset does not remove an active fictional input.

features.title: Fault indications

features.title: Confirmed disablements
features.description: Hold Next Option for three seconds to select; Enable/Disable stages a change; Next Option confirms and moves on. Exiting discards the latest unconfirmed toggle.

features.title: Access-level-3 one-man walk test
features.description: The checked engineering manual places zone-test programming behind access level three. It is not modelled as an operator button sequence here.

features.title: Coincidence
features.scope: Pairs 1/2, 3/4, 5/6, 7/8; Next Option confirms each staged choice.

features.title: Nonlatching
features.scope: Individual zones; Next Option confirms each staged choice.

features.title: Delays

features.title: Test
features.scope: Individual zones; exit level 3 before testing and restore test assignments afterward.

lessons.title: Use the real numbered access keys
lessons.summary: Practise the fascia’s actual dual-labelled number keys, then leave authorised access.

steps.instruction: Press the physical 2 / Exit access mode key to start the documented access code.
Press the dedicated number 1 key.
Press 4 / Enable-disable.
Press 3 / Next option to finish 2 1 4 3.
Press Exit access mode to return to general-user controls.

lessons.title: Check lamps using the shared key
lessons.summary: The lamp-test key is available with the controls accessed.

steps.instruction: Turn the simulated access key to I.
Press Enable/disable · Lamp test outside selection to test indicators and beeper.
Turn the key back to O.

lessons.title: Mute a fault without claiming a repair
lessons.summary: The internal buzzer can be silenced at access level one; the fault still needs investigation.

steps.instruction: Press Silence internal sounder. The zone fault stays visible.

lessons.title: Silence and resound an active alarm
lessons.summary: This exercise deliberately ends with the fictional fire still active; it does not claim the cause has cleared.

steps.instruction: Turn the simulated access key to I.
Press Silence/resound sounders. The fire indication becomes steady.
Press Silence/resound sounders again to resound the fictional alarm.

lessons.title: Clear the fictional input, then reset
lessons.summary: Reset only follows the source being cleared; an active input can bring the alarm back.

steps.instruction: Turn the simulated access key to I.
Silence the alarm sounders.
Use the training input control to return fictional zone 1 to Normal. This is not a panel key.
Press Control panel reset after the fictional cause is cleared.
Return the key to O.

lessons.title: Practise manual sounder activation
lessons.summary: The checked manual says manual sounder activation does not trigger the remote and auxiliary fire outputs.

steps.instruction: Turn the simulated key to I.
Press Silence/resound sounders to activate the fictional sounders.
Press the same key again to silence them.
Return the key to O.

lessons.title: Disable zone 1, then restore it
lessons.summary: A staged toggle and a confirmed disablement are different states; finish with the fictional zone enabled.

steps.instruction: Turn the simulated key to I.
Hold Next option for three seconds to select zone 1.
Press Enable/disable to stage the disablement.
Press Next option to confirm zone 1 and move on.
Turn the key to O to leave selection.
Return the key to I.
Hold Next option for three seconds to select the disabled zone 1.
Press Enable/disable to stage re-enabling.
Press Next option to confirm re-enabling.
Return the key to O.

lessons.title: Leave an unconfirmed toggle unchanged
lessons.summary: The manual explicitly retains only changes made before the last confirming Next option press.

steps.instruction: Turn the simulated key to I.
Hold Next option for three seconds to select zone 1.
Stage a disablement with Enable/disable, without confirming it.
Turn the key to O before pressing Next option. The unconfirmed change is discarded.

lessons.title: Remove the cover and enter level 3
lessons.summary: Use the actual internal SW8 control and Escape Access. Removing the cover alone does not enter engineering access.

steps.instruction: Remove the simulated cover to expose the Main Control PCB. This changes only the training view.
Press the internal SW8 Access Level Three Functions button once to select coincidence.
Press Escape Access (the physical 2 key) to leave engineering functions. Confirmed settings remain.
Replace the simulated cover after leaving access level 3.

lessons.title: Program and restore a coincidence pair

Press the internal SW8 Access Level Three Functions button once to select coincidence.
Press Next Option once to select the first item. The three-second user-disablement hold is not required here.
Press Enable/Disable to stage the opposite setting.
Press Next Option to confirm the selected setting and move on.
Press Escape Access (the physical 2 key) to leave engineering functions. Confirmed settings remain.
Press the internal SW8 Access Level Three Functions button once to select coincidence.
Press Next Option once to select the first item. The three-second user-disablement hold is not required here.
Press Enable/Disable to stage returning pair 1/2 to independent operation.
Press Next Option to confirm the selected setting and move on.
Press Escape Access (the physical 2 key) to leave engineering functions. Confirmed settings remain.
Replace the simulated cover after leaving access level 3.

lessons.title: Program a non-latching zone, then restore it

Press Next Option once to select the first item. The three-second user-disablement hold is not required here.

Press Next Option to confirm the selected setting and move on.
Press Escape Access (the physical 2 key) to leave engineering functions. Confirmed settings remain.

Press Next Option once to select the first item. The three-second user-disablement hold is not required here.

Press Enable/Disable to stage the opposite setting.

Press Escape Access (the physical 2 key) to leave engineering functions. Confirmed settings remain.
Press the internal SW8 Access Level Three Functions button 3 times to select delays.
Press Next Option once to select the first item. The three-second user-disablement hold is not required here.
Press Enable/Disable to stage the opposite setting.
Press Next Option to confirm the selected setting and move on.
Press Next Option seven times to pass unchanged zones 2–8 and select Remote Output.
Press Enable/Disable to stage the opposite setting.
Press Next Option to confirm the selected setting and move on.
Press Enable/Disable to stage the opposite setting.
Press Next Option to confirm the selected setting and move on.

Press Escape Access (the physical 2 key) to leave engineering functions. Confirmed settings remain.

lessons.title: Put zone 1 into walk test and restore it
lessons.summary: Leave access level 3 before testing. The manual describes approximately one second sounding and eight seconds off; this is a simulated timing demonstration.

steps.instruction: Remove the simulated cover to expose the Main Control PCB. This changes only the training view.
Press the internal SW8 Access Level Three Functions button 4 times to select test.
Press Next Option once to select the first item. The three-second user-disablement hold is not required here.
Press Enable/Disable to stage the opposite setting.
Press Next Option to confirm the selected setting and move on.
Press Escape Access (the physical 2 key) to leave engineering functions. Confirmed settings remain.
Apply a fictional detector/MCP input to the zone in test.

Press the internal SW8 Access Level Three Functions button 4 times to select test.

lessons.title: Choose whether a new zone resounds
lessons.summary: Sounder Status uses three quick flashes then a longer gap for resound, and equal on/off periods for no resound. The toggle is direct in this function.

steps.instruction: Remove the simulated cover to expose the Main Control PCB. This changes only the training view.
Press the internal SW8 Access Level Three Functions button 9 times to select sounder status.
Press Enable/Disable to select no resound for an alarm in a new zone. Observe the equal on/off pattern.
Press Enable/Disable again to restore the training default: a new zone resounds, shown by three quick flashes then a gap.
Press Escape Access (the physical 2 key) to leave engineering functions. Confirmed settings remain.
Replace the simulated cover after leaving access level 3.

lessons.title: Read the four engineering diagnostic views
lessons.summary: Synthetic faults distinguish zone circuits, a system code and a repeater number. These read-only views do not identify a physical cable-break location or prove a repair.

steps.instruction: Remove the simulated cover to expose the Main Control PCB. This changes only the training view.
Create a fictional open-circuit indication on zone 2.
Create a fictional short-circuit indication on zone 4.
Create a fictional watchdog system fault.
Create a fictional fault at repeater 3.
Press SW8 five times to reach System Fault. Zone Fault indicator 1 identifies the documented watchdog code here.
Press SW8 once for Repeater Fault. Indicator 3 now means repeater 3, not detector zone 3.
Press SW8 once for Open Circuit. The zone 2 fault indicator identifies the fictional open circuit.
Press SW8 once for Short Circuit. The zone 4 fault indicator identifies the fictional short circuit.
Press Escape Access (the physical 2 key) to leave engineering functions. Confirmed settings remain.
Clear the fictional zone 2 fault source.
Clear the fictional zone 4 fault source.
Clear the synthetic watchdog fault source; this is a training input, not a physical repair.
Clear the synthetic repeater 3 fault source.
Turn the simulated enable key to I for the documented reset control.
Press Reset after clearing the synthetic source. System faults need their own reset/check rather than an automatic repair claim.
Return the simulated key to O.
Replace the simulated cover after leaving access level 3.

profiles.title: Sigma CP
profiles.variant: K11080M2 eight-zone K-series; sigma_CP 214.hex or later warning scope — Man-1078 Issue 25
profiles.scope: Source-reviewed fascia, operator controls, Write Enable access-level-3 set/review functions and guided conventional-zone call-outs.
limitations: A fictional eight-zone K11080M2 K-series fixture with common alarm operation. It is not a T-series wiring or CP-A AlarmSense simulator.

This conventional panel identifies circuits by zone, not individual addressed detectors. Disablement affects the whole selected zone. Adding or replacing a detector is circuit work followed by checks and testing; there is no detector enrolment menu.
Active-device warning on a disabled zone is scoped to sigma_CP 214.hex or later, as stated by the main manual. It is not assumed for older panels.

The operator manuals do not establish the complete MODE cycle order. An explicit training target chooser avoids inventing a hardware press count. Engineering start, wrap and alphabetic code-entry details are also not fully documented.
Page 16 says move Write Enable to the right for access level 3, while page 19 calls the normal/off position right. The trainer uses ON/OFF labels and does not assert a switch direction.

The manual describes Enter setting an engineering option and a flashing dot showing that it is set; it does not explicitly describe unsetting it with a second press. Restore training configuration is a separate simulation action, not a hardware button sequence.

Test auto-reset is described only as after a few seconds. Non-latching zones may take up to 20 seconds to reset when sounders operate. Advancing the training clock or test cycle does not certify a measured hardware timer.

Removing or refitting the simulated cover does not change Write Enable or erase settings. The cover-off illustration shows the source panel plate and switch aperture, not an invented view of the full cabinet, power supply or batteries.

Only supported configuration effects are simulated. T-series/zonal sounder, ancillary-board, intrinsically safe barrier, short-circuit threshold and unverified version-specific options remain reference-only. No live electrical work, detector compatibility decision or real repair is certified.

The source user guide has an Issue 06 cover and _05 page footers. The newer Issue 25 main manual is primary; saved/downloaded Sigma records are not hash-pinned by the archive and their edition must be checked.

features.title: Enable Control key
features.description: At access level one, only buzzer silence and lamp test are available. The Enable Control key makes operator buttons available.

features.title: Lamp test without access key
features.description: Lamp test operates at any time; the user guide says the buzzer sounds whilst the button is pressed.

features.title: Alarm, silence and reset
features.description: Common Fire lights and zonal Fire flashes; silence makes the zonal fire indication steady. The sounder key toggles silence/resound.

features.title: Fault indications
features.description: Show zone, sounder and power fault indications without diagnosing the exact hardware cause.

features.title: Documented d target
features.description: At d plus a selected zone, Enter toggles disablement. A disabled zone with an active input must not be presented as harmless to re-enable.

features.title: Documented db target
features.description: At db, Enter toggles all sounders disabled/enabled and the general/sounder disablement indicators.

features.title: Documented t target
features.description: At t plus a selected zone, Enter toggles test mode. The automatic reset interval is not numerically specified by the source.

features.title: Mode cycle order not verified
features.description: The target chooser is an explicit training shortcut; it does not claim a manufacturer MODE cycle order or number of presses.

features.title: Configured detector and call-point delays
features.description: Supported engineering time and zone-source settings become active only when operator Ad is enabled. The default fictional configuration has no active delay.

features.title: Write Enable access level 3
features.description: Internal switch grants engineering configuration independently of removing the cover. ON/OFF avoid the conflicting printed direction.

features.title: Source-backed configuration set and review
features.description: Numeric +10/+1 and Enter set supported options; the flashing units dot identifies a set option. Reference-only codes remain identified without simulating their unsupported hardware effects.

features.title: Internal fault indications
features.description: Synthetic diagnostic causes distinguish the documented internal lamps. Watchdog reset is a conceptual source-named internal control; its exact position is not asserted.

features.title: Conventional detector work
features.description: Disabling a detector means isolating its whole zone. Add/replace practice records only a fictional checkpoint and then exercises zone test/restoration; it never enrols an addressed detector.

lessons.title: Test indicators with controls locked

lessons.summary: Practise the front-panel key access without entering engineering configuration.

steps.instruction: Turn the simulated Enable Control key on.
Turn the key off again; only buzzer silence and lamp test remain available.

lessons.summary: The fire remains active at the end of this exercise.

lessons.title: Clear the fictional cause before resetting

Silence the fictional alarm sounders.

Press Mode to open the documented-target training chooser. The hardware cycle order is not verified.
Choose the documented zone-disablement target d (starting at zone 1). This is a training shortcut.
Press Enter to disable the selected zone 1.

Turn the Enable Control key off.

lessons.title: Use documented db to restore sounders

steps.instruction: Turn the Enable Control key on.

lessons.title: Add or replace a detector — panel practice
lessons.summary: A conventional detector has no panel enrolment menu. Practise the zone controls around fictional detector work: isolation, a clearly synthetic work checkpoint, test and restoration. Exact detector/base compatibility and real work remain separate checks.

steps.instruction: Turn the Enable Control key ON.
Press Mode to open the documented-target training chooser.
Choose d using the training shortcut. The whole zone, including other connected detectors/call points, is affected.
Press Enter at d1 to disable the entire fictional zone 1. This is not individual device isolation.

Record the fictional work checkpoint only. In the real installation, check the exact compatible detector/base and circuit arrangement; this trainer neither adds an addressed device nor certifies physical work.
Set the fictional zone 1 input to Normal for this exercise. This input control is not evidence of a real electrical test.
Press Enter at d1 to re-enable the fictional zone. Check the displayed state rather than assuming key-off removes disablements.
Press Mode to open the documented-target training chooser.
Choose t using the training shortcut for the fictional zone 1 test.
Press Enter at t1 to put zone 1 in test.
Activate the fictional detector input in the test zone.
Clear the fictional test input.
Advance the labelled training test cycle. The manual says automatic reset occurs after a few seconds; no exact hardware timer is claimed.
Press Enter at t1 to take zone 1 out of test.
Turn the Enable Control key OFF and check the fictional panel has no introduced test or disablement.

lessons.title: Read internal faults and a watchdog indication
lessons.summary: Distinguish fictional Mains fail and CPU watchdog indications. A conceptual Watchdog reset is source-named but its physical position is not mapped by the checked figure.

steps.instruction: Introduce a fictional loss-of-mains indication. This changes a training input only.
Open the simulated cover to reach Write Enable.
Clear the fictional mains-failure cause after reading the internal Mains fail description. No live supply test is represented.
Introduce a fictional watchdog event. CPU/System Fault stays latched until the documented Watchdog reset.
Clear the fictional watchdog cause. Its recorded indication remains latched; clearing this training cause is not a physical repair.
Press the separately labelled conceptual Watchdog reset. The source names this internal control but does not map its exact position.
Refit the simulated cover after checking Write Enable is OFF.

engineering.entryDirectionNote: Issue 25 page 16 describes RIGHT for entry but page 19 also calls RIGHT normal/off. ON/OFF are deliberate neutral labels; physical direction is not asserted.
engineering.selectionNote: Mode +10 and Select +1 enter numeric codes. The exact initial display, wrap and alphabetic-bank entry sequence are not established. Code 00 is an explicit fictional starting point; Choose code is a labelled training assist.
engineering.unsetNote: Enter sets/reviews a source-backed option. The checked source does not explicitly say a second Enter unsets it. Restore training configuration is a separate fictional reset and preserves other local records.
engineering.warningNote: The source marks codes 21,22,71–78,81–88,A1–A8 and E1–E8 as not complying with EN54-2.
engineering.timingNote: Three buzzer pips every few seconds indicate level3. Exact cadence is not claimed. Zone-test reset is after a few seconds; non-latching reset can take up to 20 seconds when sounders operate.
engineering.coverNote: Opening or refitting the simulated door does not operate Write Enable. Leave the switch OFF after practice; the source says General Fault remains lit if it is left ON.

diagnostics.label: Mains fail
diagnostics.scope: AC supply absent; panel running on batteries.

diagnostics.label: Batt fail
diagnostics.scope: Battery disconnected or charging circuit high resistance/failure; one lamp does not identify a particular failed component.

diagnostics.label: CPU fault
diagnostics.scope: Watchdog event latched; source requires Watchdog reset. A synthetic reset is not proof of hardware repair.

diagnostics.label: Aux 24V fault
diagnostics.scope: Auxiliary-output protection operated; physical load/protection behaviour is outside this trainer.

diagnostics.label: Batt low
diagnostics.scope: Low standby battery indication; the trainer does not measure battery voltage.

diagnostics.label: Earth fault
diagnostics.scope: System wiring earth indication; no cable location is inferred.

diagnostics.label: System fuse fault
diagnostics.scope: System supply protection indication; the trainer does not operate physical fuses.

diagnostics.label: S1 fault
diagnostics.scope: Open or short on sounder circuit1; the indication does not distinguish the break location.

diagnostics.label: S2 fault
diagnostics.scope: Open or short on sounder circuit2; the indication does not distinguish the break location.

diagnostics.label: Comms fault
diagnostics.scope: Communication lost with a repeater or ancillary board; no accessory enrolment is simulated.

callOuts.title: Disable a detector’s zone
callOuts.summary: Temporarily disable and restore the circuit containing a detector.
callOuts.scope: Sigma CP is conventional: d1–d8 disable a whole zone, not an individual addressed device. Confirm the affected zone and all devices it serves.

callOuts.title: Add / replace a detector
callOuts.summary: Practise the panel-side isolation, test and restoration around detector work.
callOuts.scope: No detector enrolment or Add device menu exists for this conventional zone. Exact detector/base compatibility and physical circuit work are separate; the lesson checkpoint is fictional, never proof of work completed.

callOuts.title: Put a zone into test
callOuts.summary: Select the documented t code, test flag and deliberate restoration.
callOuts.scope: Test mode affects the chosen conventional zone. An automatic-reset demonstration does not certify a live detector test.

callOuts.title: Find an internal fault indication
callOuts.summary: Read the source descriptions for internal faults and practise a watchdog indication.
callOuts.scope: Internal lamps narrow the indicated subsystem; they do not prove a failed component, repaired cause or cable-break position.

callOuts.title: Review level-3 configuration
callOuts.summary: Open the cover, use Write Enable and inspect the displayed option and set dot.
callOuts.scope: Use the exact manual and record existing settings before changes. Conditional codes stay reference-only; training reset is not a physical unset procedure.
